items.q: How did Ferriss research The 4-Hour Body?
items.a: He **stress-tested absolutes** ("always", "never") and looked at tech only small groups used, like early wearables and continuous glucose monitors.

items.q: What three questions does he ask experts?
items.a: **What nerds do at night**, what rich people do now that millions will do in ten years, and **where people cobble together awkward solutions**.
No. The future is already here, **not evenly distributed**, so he looks for germinating seeds.

items.q: What is hypergraphia in his process?
items.a: He **records almost everything in writing**, so past notes can be examined and replicated.

items.q: Why move to a dense hub for a season?
items.a: It gives a **high surface area for luck**: many serendipitous encounters across disciplines, worth **3 to 6 months** or longer.

items.q: How did he get noticed as a volunteer?
items.a: He did **more than the bare minimum**: carrying water, taking out garbage and checking badges at startup events.

items.q: Why not ask someone to be your mentor?
items.a: It sounds like a **never-ending free life-coach commitment**; learn from almost anyone and ask for something specific.

items.q: How does he use friends as models?
items.a: He asks **"what would Matt do?"** when emotion takes over, and hires coaches or therapists for accountability.

items.q: What is the Past Year Review?
items.a: Go through **every week of last year** and note people, places and activities with peak positive or negative emotion.

items.q: What comes out of the review?
items.a: A **do-more / do-less list**, with the do-more items booked in the calendar immediately.

items.q: Why schedule the important things first?
items.a: **The urgent will crush the important** if it is not on the calendar.
He gives days a theme, such as **Monday for admin**, and keeps exercise after lunch.
Roughly **10 pm to 4 am**, riding the wave when in the zone and sleeping when not.

items.q: What does "make pain part of your medicine" mean?
items.a: Turn your own hard history into **credibility that helps one person**, not necessarily the whole world.
